cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Retroactive Permission
cards.instruction: Get approval for something you have already done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've invited six people to dinner. You used to panic over two; my hosting lessons have brought you a long way. Is six all right?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We still only have two chairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You're checking numbers before menus, just as I taught you. I'll borrow the extra seats.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And cook? I'm not feeding six people while you collect chairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll do both. You can practice the welcome I taught you. Does that make the invitations a yes?

reason: Preserve the useful Drive exchange while replacing generic training prefaces with specific corrections, qualified praise and claimed influence that make the mentor role determine A's tactic.
